did_you_know.text: Haman son of Hammedatha the Agagite was given an exceptionally high position by King Ahasuerus: his throne was placed above the thrones of all the officials who were with him.
All the king’s servants at the king’s gate were ordered to kneel and bow down to Haman, but Mordecai neither knelt nor bowed down.
After Mordecai refused to comply with them day after day, the king’s servants reported to Haman that Mordecai was a Jew.
Haman was not satisfied with harming Mordecai alone; he sought to destroy all the Jews throughout the entire kingdom of Ahasuerus.
Haman cast the pur, that is, the lot, in the month of Nisan, in the twelfth year of King Ahasuerus’s reign, to determine when to carry out his plan; the lot selected the month of Adar.
To persuade the king, Haman described the Jews as a scattered and separate people whose customs were different and who did not obey the king’s laws.
Haman offered to pay ten thousand talents of silver into the royal treasury if the decree against the Jews was approved.
The king gave Haman his signet ring, thereby granting him authority to act in the king’s name and seal royal decrees.
The decree was written in the king’s name and sealed with the king’s ring, then sent to the satraps, governors, and officials of the peoples in every province, in its own script and language.
The couriers set out urgently to spread the decree, but while the king and Haman sat down to drink, the city of Susa was bewildered and confused.
